parts:
sapply is mostly intended for interactive use and it will perform conversions based on some internal oracle that knows best what the function should do. Maybe use lapply or vapply instead. I don't see anything wrong with the results, so you may have to tell me what you expected. Since the difference is in that paste call, I would look into sep and collapse args and see if you need one of those (just a guess here, sorry if you have already).


Antonio

Hi,
thanks for the reproducible code! I started a fresh R session loaded rmr2 and switched to the local backend

rmr.options(backend = "local")

then set to debug the reducer

debug(tfm.reduce)

and run the last MR job again. I don't know why anyone who can reproduce a problem on a small input wouldn't want to try this approach. Clearly I am not sending out the message in the right way, and not for lack of trying. 
The first thing I noticed is that v1 is sometimes a matrix, sometimes a vector (key 1). That's what you get for using sapply. If you don't believe me, this is what uber-R programer Hadley Wickham, author of half of CRAN, has to say about it in his Advanced R book:  "sapply() is great for interactive use because it saves typing, but if you use it inside your functions you’ll get weird errors if you supply the wrong type of input." 
Mixing matrix and vector output is not supported in rmr. Once you output one keyval with arg types T1 and T2, all the following ones should have the same type. For matrices and data.frames, also the number of columns should be the same, and also the type and name of columns for data frames. Try to make your reducer satisfy this and I think it will start working correctly.
